approach: Teach the plurals where the written accent appears or disappears (joven → jóvenes, inglés → ingleses), the nouns that do not change (los lunes, los paraguas, los sacacorchos) and plural family surnames (los García).
coverage: The stressed syllable stays the same in the plural, so a written accent may appear or disappear
Accent appears: joven → jóvenes, examen → exámenes, imagen → imágenes
Accent disappears: canción → canciones, inglés → ingleses, autobús → autobuses
Words ending in an unstressed vowel + s do not change: el lunes → los lunes, la crisis → las crisis
Compounds ending in -s do not change: el sacacorchos → los sacacorchos, el paraguas → los paraguas
Family surnames usually stay the same: los García, los Pérez

blocks.purpose: States why accents move in plurals, in one idea.

data.anchor: A plural almost always keeps the stress on the same syllable as the singular, so the written accent appears or disappears to show it.
prerequisites: jo-ven → JÓ-ve-nes: adding a syllable needs an accent to keep the stress on jo.
can-CIÓN → can-CIO-nes: the stress now falls there naturally, so the accent goes.
You do not need the full accent rules yet: learn these common pairs.

trapReasons.1: The singular has no accent, so the plural seems not to need one.

data.whyIntuitionFailed: Learners copy the singular spelling and just add -es.
data.correctReasoning: The stress stays on jo. With the extra syllable, that stress needs a written accent: jóvenes.
data.recoveryTip: joven → jóvenes, examen → exámenes: the accent appears.

blocks.purpose: Closes with the stress rule and the unchanging nouns.

data.takeaway: The stress stays put (with rare exceptions such as carácter, caracteres), so accents appear (jóvenes, exámenes) or disappear (canciones, ingleses); words like lunes, paraguas and family names stay the same.
